title: The First Atom: Big Bang as Physical Projection of Ontological Axioms
honest_boundary: The explanation is structurally coherent and empirically consistent, but the ontological grounding (A1.3) is not formally derived; it remains an interpretive mapping.
overstatement_risks: C017: CMB as 'receipt' of information storage | C027: Hydrogen as 'durable information storage' | C032: CMB as 'cost-of-coherence' | C033: 'Every binding event' claim | C036: 'First transaction' | C041: 'photon's timestamp IS the first tick of physical time' | C044: 'record makes time real' | C050: 'universe's first act of seeing' | C056: 'fine-tuning numbers protect the axiom chain'
kill_conditions: If the strong force coupling constant is not fine-tuned to 1% for hydrogen stability, the projection fails. | If recombination is not the first stable distinction, the mapping to A1.3 fails. | If the CMB is not consistent with T3.1, the bridge fails.
plain_summary: This source interprets the Big Bang and recombination as physical projections of ontological axioms (Existence, Distinction, Information). It argues that recombination marks the first stable distinction and thus the first durable information storage, with the CMB as evidence. The explanation is structurally coherent but relies on metaphorical language and lacks formal derivations for the axiom-to-physics mappings.
